rows.name: Restore open tabs on launch
rows.body: Reopens the query tabs you had open last time. Turn it off if your query text is sensitive — the tabs are stored in plain text.

rows.name: Query timeout
rows.body: Cancels a query still running after this long. Set it to 0 for no limit.

rows.name: Notify me when a query finishes
rows.body: Announces a finished query — a system notification if you've switched away from Downpick, an in-app notice if you haven't, never both. A query you cancelled, or one the database rejected, isn't announced: you're already looking at it. Clicking the system notification brings the window forward and opens the tab the query came from.

rows.name: Only after n seconds
rows.body: How long a query has to have run to be worth announcing. Set it to 0 to announce every one. A query stopped by the Query timeout above is exempt and always announced — being told when that limit trips is the point of setting it.

rows.name: Send a test notification
rows.body: Raises one on demand. Your operating system also has to allow notifications from Downpick, and one it blocks is turned away silently — nothing inside the app can detect that, so firing one and looking is the only honest check.

rows.name: Vault file path
rows.body: Where the encrypted vault lives — point it at an encrypted drive if you like. Browse… opens a vault you already have and New location… chooses where a new one goes, or type the path yourself, filename included. Changing it locks the current vault; the file at the new path has its own master password, and one is created if nothing is there yet. The same choice is offered on first launch, before any vault exists.

rows.name: Change master password
rows.body: Re-encrypts the vault key under a new password and deletes the previous backup file, which is still readable with the old password.

rows.name: Auto-lock
rows.body: Re-locks the vault and closes every open connection after this much inactivity. It tracks app activity rather than mouse movement, so a long query is never interrupted by its own timer.
